clue.text: Ways to give boats horsepower

parts.note: canal barges were once hauled along by horses walking the bank beside the water, so the routes literally supplied power from horses

explanation.surface: A question of how to make boats faster by fitting more powerful engines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horsepower' suggests engine output; here it is real horses pulling barges along the canal bank.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the paths beside canals along which horses walked while hauling barges.

clue.text: Carpet relaid — the edges wouldn't fit

indicators.note: laid again in a new pattern, so the letters that follow are rearranged
the edges of the word the are just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A fitter grumbles that a carpet laid a second time still won't sit right at the borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the edges' gives TE, the outside letters of 'the'; 'relaid' shuffles TE with WOULDNTFIT. A TUFTED WILTON is a type of woven carpet named after the Wiltshire town of Wilton.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kind of pile floor covering made in Wilton, Wiltshire, with tufted loops.

clue.text: See 5
Broken foremast with its end near the stern

annotationWithheld.why: Broken foremast with its end near the stern: AFTERMOST is an anagram of FOREMAST plus T, but T is the end of 'foremast' itself ('its end'), so 'foremast' is both the fodder and the source of the extra letter
annotationWithheld.clue: Broken foremast with its end near the stern

clue.text: Change to oyster shells for presentation of Meals On Wheels

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters of to oyster shells are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap a dish to oysters for a catering service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meals On Wheels' is really a meal served from a wheeled cart, not the charity delivery service. A HOSTESS TROLLEY is a heated serving cart popular in British homes in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: This heated wheeled cart keeps dishes warm and rolls them to the dining table for serving.

clue.text: Country's tiny capital city featured in extremely worthy publication

indicators.note: to be featured in something is to appear inside it, so these pieces sit within the outer letters
the extremes of worthy are its first and last letters

parts.note: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula, here in its possessive form
tiny means wee, a Scottish and informal word for small
KL is the common abbreviation for Kuala Lumpur, capital of Malaysia

explanation.surface: A small nation's capital gets a feature in a respectable magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' keeps only the outside letters of 'worthy'. The answer is a long-running British magazine for women, and the puzzle pays tribute to the comedian Victoria Wood.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a long-established British magazine aimed at female readers.

clue.text: Natural defence is down under cardinal

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia, the land down under
one is a cardinal number

explanation.surface: A senior churchman in Australia is said to be a natural protector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like a churchman but means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer shields the earth from ultraviolet radiation, a protection supplied by nature.

clue.text: Paid Nato loose change

indicators.note: something loose is not held in place, so the letters of Paid Nato are rearranged

explanation.surface: NATO was paid in loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose change' reads as coins; 'loose' is the anagram signal and 'change' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaption is an alternative form of adaptation, an alteration to suit new conditions.

clue.text: Smoke joint when leading man replaces drug

indicators.note: one thing replaces another when it takes its place, so a letter is swapped

parts.note: the shoulder is a joint of the body
H is slang for heroin

indicators.note: the leading letter of man is its first

explanation.surface: Someone lights up a joint after a drug is swapped by the lead actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette, which suits 'Smoke'; here it is the shoulder. The M from 'leading man' replaces the H in SHOULDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn slowly and give off smoke without flame.

clue.text: Singers fast leaving harmful intensive care and ringing Ireland

indicators.note: when one thing is leaving another it is taken out of it

parts.note: malevolent means wishing or doing harm
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
IC is a common abbreviation for intensive care
an echo is a sound ringing back

explanation.surface: A patient leaves intensive care quickly while bells ring across Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but is LENT, removed from MALEVOLENT to leave MALEVO.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice choir is a group of singers made up of men, a Welsh tradition.

clue.text: Selfies tastelessy expose celebrations

indicators.note: to expose is to reveal, so the answer is laid bare within the run of letters

explanation.surface: Tasteless selfies show off people's parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'tastelessy', a slip for 'tastelessly' that does not affect the letters used.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiestas are festive occasions or holidays, especially in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Green party follows a detail of speech

indicators.note: follows places the piece after what comes before
read as de-tail, take the last letter off

parts.note: vocal means relating to the voice or speech
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A green party pays attention to a small point in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' means remove the tail: VOCAL loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is a shade of dull green named after the fruit's skin and flesh.

clue.text: Euclid's first rule confounded by mathematician

indicators.note: the first letter of Euclid's is its opening one
confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters of rule are rearranged

explanation.surface: Euclid's leading principle was baffling to a mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Euclid' tempts as the definition, but the mathematician is EULER (Leonhard Euler, Swiss).
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss scholar of numbers and geometry.

clue.text: Basic loss of mass from the Spanish cheese

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: loss of means the letter is removed

parts.note: Emmental is a Swiss cheese with holes
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A simple account of a Spanish cheese losing weight.
explanation.walkthrough: EMMENTAL loses one M.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or rudimentary, relating to first principles.

clue.text: Risks all and attacks chap who's changed sides

parts.note: goes for means attacks

indicators.note: switching from left to right swaps an L for an R

parts.note: bloke is informal British for a man or chap

explanation.surface: Someone gambles everything and attacks a defector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed sides' swaps L (left) for R (right) in BLOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for broke is an idiom for staking everything on one attempt.

clue.text: Battle mask

definitions.meaning: An 1854 Crimean War engagement, the one with the Charge of the Light Brigade
a woollen hood covering head and face

explanation.definitionFit: The knitted head covering took its name from the Crimean battle where soldiers wore them.

clue.text: Insular Magna Carta spirit

annotationWithheld.why: Insular Magna Carta spirit: ARMAGNAC is hidden in 'insular Magna Carta', but the only hidden-word signal is the 'in' at the start of 'insular', so that word is both fodder and indicator

clue.text: Maybe making light of natural disaster

definitions.meaning: in Genesis God said let there be light, so creating light is an example of something done by the deity
in insurance language, an unforeseeable natural catastrophe such as a flood

explanation.definitionFit: Insurers use the phrase for events beyond human control, and Genesis credits creating light to the deity.

clue.text: Loaded short container of coal (none left) with a measure of shaking

parts.note: loaded is slang for wealthy

indicators.note: a container holds something inside it, so the next piece goes within

parts.note: terse means short or curt

indicators.note: left means departed, so a letter is removed

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A wealthy person's small coal box, now empty, along with a gauge of tremors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'none left' means the nought has gone from the fuel; 'with a' is just a link. The scale is named after the seismologist Charles Richter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Richter scale is the logarithmic scale for rating earthquake magnitude.

clue.text: Dangerous gas support for reproductive equipment

parts.note: CO is carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas
a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: A toxic gas holds up equipment for breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproductive' suggests biology; here it means making copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopier reproduces documents, so it is equipment for making copies.

clue.text: See 1 down
Like followers of trashy soap to start loving its characters

indicators.note: trashy means rubbishy, so the letters of soap are knocked about
the start of each of these words is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fan of a trashy soap opera grows to love its cast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Like followers', meaning like the apostles who followed Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostolic means relating to the apostles, Christ's original disciples.

clue.text: Result of adding to central Italy

indicators.note: the central letters of Italy are those without its ends

explanation.surface: Adding something to the middle of Italy produces a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central Italy' gives TAL, the middle of ITALY.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the sum reached when numbers are added together.

clue.text: Rejected some plastic orchid flowers

indicators.note: Rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some artificial orchids were turned down as decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Croci is a plural of crocus, the spring bulb with cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Close connection provides protection for retired woman

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is a link or connection

explanation.surface: A close relationship gives security to a woman who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests stopping work; here it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress covers a woman who has gone to bed for the night.

clue.text: Slimming aid — Eton mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of aid Eton are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diet aid called Eton mess, the cream-and-meringue pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON MESS is a British dessert of meringue, cream and strawberries, hardly slimming.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on a diet is to be eating less to lose weight.

clue.text: Comfort from dead ends in tricky clue

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
tricky means awkward, so the letters of clue are rearranged
the ends of dead are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A solver takes consolation from the dead ends met in a hard clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead ends' looks like a single idea, blind alleys; it gives DD, the outer letters of 'dead', placed inside CULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuddle is a hug given to console or reassure.

clue.text: Hearing score in rehearsal

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
a run is a score in cricket

explanation.surface: A court hearing scores well in a practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests listening; here it is a legal hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a practice test before the real thing.
